subject: Renewal concession request — Seneca Bridge Systems (Dec renewal)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal concession request — Seneca Bridge Systems (Dec renewal)

Hi Laura / Vivek,

Quick summary: Seneca Bridge (current ARR $420,000) is up for renewal on 2026-12-20. They've signaled a strong intent to move to a competitor unless we provide concessions. Procurement is pushing for a sub-300k number. Customer is strategic (logistics sector, potential expansion in EU next year).

What customer is asking: 20% one-year discount on seats, a $25,000 one-time SLA credit for past infra incidents, and a reset to monthly billing for the first 6 months. They've also asked for waived onboarding fees for a new module.

Why we should consider: Risk of churn with an existing multi-year relationship; new TCO from competitor includes managed migration credits. If we lose them we may forfeit an expected $1.1M ARR expansion pipeline in 2027.

Requested ask to Deal Desk / Execs: approval to offer the following as a renewal save package: 20% discount on base ARR for 12 months, $25k SLA credit, waive onboarding fee, and 6-month monthly billing cadence with standard T&Cs otherwise. I'm attaching a short proposed terms doc and the customer email thread.

Attachments: proposed_concession_terms.pdf (PDF, 98KB)

Timing: The customer needs an answer by close of day Thursday (2026-12-09) to keep the procurement runway open.

Deal details (brief):
- Deal ID: RDW-2026-1567
- Current ARR: $420,000
- Renewal term: 12 months (auto-renew)
- Renewal date: 2026-12-20

Next steps I need from you:
1) Quick read on whether the proposed concession is on-brand and acceptable.
2) If not, what is the maximum concession we can sign off without Exec approval so I can push that first?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

— Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal concession request — Seneca Bridge Systems (Dec renewal)

Thanks Aditya — noted. A few follow-ups before I escalate to Execs:

1) Please include a one-page financial impact showing net ARR impact over 12 and 24 months (with and without the concession). I need to see payback and churn risk quantified.
2) Who on the customer side owns the renewal approval? Procurement or the BU lead? If procurement is engaged, we usually require a signed mutual action plan.
3) Is this customer on a standard enterprise contract or do we have prior amendments that change renewal terms?

I took a quick look at the proposed_concession_terms.pdf — the $25k SLA credit seems high relative to annual support revenue. If this goes to Execs, we'll likely ask for a lower SLA credit and a time-limited discount.

Please attach the customer thread and any procurement correspondence. I'll prep an Exec summary if we need to push this up.

— Laura
Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal concession request — Seneca Bridge Systems (Dec renewal)

Laura — attached the requested items. Highlights below. Attaching customer_email_thread.eml (select excerpts).

Key points:
- Procurement (procurement@senecabridge.com) is leading and has a hard deadline of 2026-12-09.
- BU lead (Sam Torres) will sign if procurement confirms price.
- Customer has a competing offer that includes migration credits and 18% discount; they've signaled willingness to move quickly.
- Net ARR math: with 20% discount (year 1) our expected ARR drops to $336,000. With the $25k one-time credit the first-year net revenue impact is ~-$109,000 compared to current. However the retention preserves expansion upside.

Customer ask excerpt:
"We like Redwood's performance, but procurement has flagged the price. If you can match the competitor economics (discount + migration credit), we can sign before our year-end procurement window." — Priya Reddy

Attachments: customer_email_thread.eml (EML, 45KB)

If we need to trim: my preference is to offer 15% discount + $15k SLA credit + waive onboarding fee, but keep standard annual billing. That reduces the near-term hit while keeping renewal desk off the escalator. If Execs insist, I'm prepared to offer full 20% but want Exec signoff for the $25k SLA credit and monthly billing reset.

— Aditya
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal concession request — Seneca Bridge Systems (Dec renewal)

Folks — forwarding for Exec attention.

Quick take from Deal Desk: customer is strategic with higher-than-average expansion potential. Aditya recommends full concession but suggests a negotiated middle ground (15% + $15k SLA credit).

Proposed Exec ask: approval to offer the middle-ground package without additional signoffs: 15% discount on base ARR for 12 months, $15,000 one-time SLA credit, waive onboarding fee. No change to standard term length (12 months), and require a signed amendment with a 30-day payment term.

Business rationale in short: preserves core relationship, lowers immediate churn risk, retains expansion upside, and caps our one-time financial exposure to roughly $78k first year. If we decline, probability of churn appears >60% per Aditya.

Please respond with Approve / Reject / Counter with the fastest possible turn-around — customer expects an answer this week.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Sales — West Coast, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal concession request — Seneca Bridge Systems (Dec renewal)

Appreciate the fast work and the clear analysis. After reviewing the numbers and short-term risk, I approve the middle-ground concession with the following binding conditions: 

1) Approved package: 15% discount on base ARR for 12 months (applied at renewal), $15,000 one-time SLA credit, onboarding fee waived.
2) No monthly billing cadence reset — keep standard annual billing.
3) Customer must sign the Amendment (link below) and commit to a 12-month renewal term and a joint mutual action plan with Milestones within 10 business days of execution.
4) Legal to include a clawback clause: if customer terminates within 90 days for cause, the discount/SLA credit will be pro-rated and reclaimed.

Operational items: Laura, please prepare the Amendment and updated Quote reflecting the approved package. Aditya — communicate the approved offer to the customer with the conditions and set expectation for signature cadence. Vivek — track the HubSpot deal and mark the concession as a one-time Executive-approved exception.

Links: HubSpot Deal — https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/RDW-2026-1567
DocuSign Amendment (placeholder) — https://www.docusign.com/rdw/seneca-amendment-1567

Approved by: Marissa Cole, VP Sales
marissa.cole@redwood.com
